prompt: In `style={[a, b, c]}`, which object wins when two of them set `color`?

choices.text: The first one, as the base style
choices.why: Later objects override earlier ones.

choices.text: The most specific one, as in CSS
choices.why: There is no specificity here.

choices.text: The later one
choices.why: Right: the order in the array is the only precedence.

choices.text: Neither: React Native reports a conflict and uses the platform's default colour
choices.why: Nothing reports a conflict; the later value is used.

prompt: What does `StyleSheet.create` add over writing the same object inline?

choices.text: Types, and a place to read the styles
choices.why: Right: it returns the same object, typed; the rest is convention.

choices.text: Selectors that match by class
choices.why: There are no selectors.

choices.text: A cascade, so children inherit the styles
choices.why: There is no cascade either way.

choices.text: Media queries
choices.why: Those do not exist; the window is read with a hook.

prompt: A View holds three children and no style. How are they laid out?

choices.text: Side by side, left to right, as a flex row on the web
choices.why: The default direction here is column.

choices.text: In a grid
choices.why: There is no grid layout.

choices.text: On top of each other, in the same place
choices.why: That needs `position: "absolute"`.

choices.text: Stacked top to bottom
choices.why: Right: `flexDirection` defaults to `column`.

prompt: A row 300 points wide holds two children with `flex: 1` and `flex: 2` and nothing else. How wide is the second, in points?
The planner's header is a row and needs the icon and the title centred vertically. Which property does it?

choices.text: `justifyContent: "center"`, which centres along the main axis
choices.why: In a row the main axis is horizontal.

choices.text: `alignItems: "center"`
choices.why: Right: the cross axis of a row is vertical.

choices.text: `textAlign: "center"` on the title
choices.why: That centres text within its own box.

choices.text: `verticalAlign: "middle"`
choices.why: That is a CSS habit, not the flex answer.

prompt: The week bar's track is 342 wide, 75 minutes are done and 50 are left. Why does no line of code compute 205?

choices.text: Because `overflow: "hidden"` measures the children
choices.why: It only clips.

choices.text: Yoga shares the width in the ratio of the two `flex` values
choices.why: Right: 75 to 50 of whatever width there is.

choices.text: Because the web build rounds every width to a multiple of five
choices.why: 205 is just 60% of 342, rounded to the point.

choices.text: Because the test sets it
choices.why: The test only checks the flex values.

prompt: A row has `height: 48` and its text is cut off for one user. What is the likely cause, and the fix?

choices.text: A bug in Yoga that a newer SDK fixes
choices.why: It is doing exactly what the style asks.

choices.text: Their phone has a low density; set `height` in `px`
choices.why: There is no `px`, and density does not change a point's size.

choices.text: Their phone is in dark mode
choices.why: Colours do not change sizes.

choices.text: A large text size in their settings; use padding, not a fixed height
choices.why: Right: `fontScale` grows the text, and a fixed height does not grow.

prompt: Where should a component that switches to two columns above 600 points read the width?

choices.text: From `useWindowDimensions`, in that component
choices.why: Right: it re-renders when the window changes.

choices.text: Once at start-up, into a constant in a shared file
choices.why: That misses rotation and split screen.

choices.text: From a media query
choices.why: Media queries do not exist here.

choices.text: From `PixelRatio.get()`
choices.why: That is density, not width.

prompt: Why is `{open && <Panel />}` usually better than `display: "none"` to hide a panel?

choices.text: `display` does not exist in React Native at all
choices.why: It exists; it keeps the element mounted.

choices.text: It is the only way a screen reader can skip the panel
choices.why: A hidden element is skipped too; the difference is that it stays mounted.

choices.text: The panel is then not in the tree at all
choices.why: Right: `display: "none"` keeps it mounted, with its state.

choices.text: It renders faster on iOS than on Android
choices.why: Not the reason.

choices.text: Dark mode needs a paid Expo plan
choices.why: Nothing here costs money.

choices.text: `useTheme` is called in the wrong component

choices.text: The palette's muted grey is too light
choices.why: The bar's text is not the palette's.

choices.text: The app's palette as an object, ready to use in styles

choices.text: A boolean, `true` in dark mode
choices.why: It returns a word.

choices.text: `"light"`, `"dark"` or `null`
choices.why: Right, and it re-renders on a switch.

choices.text: The screen's brightness
choices.why: Brightness is not exposed this way.

prompt: What does a `testID` become, and who reads it?

choices.text: The accessible name, read by screen readers
choices.why: A screen reader never announces it.

choices.text: A name for tests and tools; `data-testid` on the web

choices.text: A CSS class used to style the element on the web
choices.why: It styles nothing.

choices.text: The store listing's keyword

prompt: At 768 points wide every row stretches to 720. What would a tablet layout need that no stretch provides?
